title: The Run
audience: A 60-second paper-cut crime short for festival and phone audiences; one male narrator, no dialogue, no women on screen.
tone: terse, cold, procedural; a case file read aloud in the rain, never a melodrama
logline: A man kills in the rain and runs for ten days; a detective's file, a checkpoint lamp and a gray hat close the circle, and the calendar never reaches eleven.

spine.want: to get away with the murder and stay ahead of the file
spine.obstacle: the detective's file, the checkpoint lamp and a city that keeps his face
spine.turn: he leaves his gray hat on the checkpoint barrier, and the detective follows the hat to the bridge
spine.button: the calendar never reaches eleven: day ten ends in the yard, and the noose is only a shadow

narration.text: Day one. Rain on the bricks. A knife, a coat, a body under a sheet.
By dawn the file was open, and his name was in it.
Days two and three. He ran through rain; the city kept his face.
Day four. A train, a tunnel, a ticket on a seat in the dark.
Days five and six. A rented room, a calendar, a door he did not answer.
Day seven. The page turned. He counted the hours, not the money.
Day eight. A checkpoint at the city's edge, and a lamp found his face.
He turned his collar up and walked through the light without stopping.
Day nine. The bridge was wet, and the detective waited at the far end.
The cuffs closed. The city went on behind him, indifferent.
Day ten. A cell, a file, a judge, and a sentence read without hurry.
The gavel fell. The warder took his arm, and the court was empty.
They brought him back to the same cell, and the calendar still said ten.
At dawn they walked him to the yard, where the noose was a shadow.
